title: What story can an expression tell?
description: Three expressions are turned into short stories, one term of the expression for each part of the story, and then each value is found. The video checks each story by working backwards.
teaching_notes: One idea: each term of the expression is one thing that happens in the story, and the sign tells whether it is added or taken away. Many stories fit, so ask the child to make one of their own.

video_script.why: The child goes from an expression back to a story, matching each term to one event, as the dosa expression matched dosas and tip.
video_script.substitution: Change the things in the story and the method stays the same: one term for each part, the sign for coming in or going out.
video_script.anchor: three expressions in a column on the board: 89 + 21 − 10, 5 × 12 − 6 and 4 × 9 + 2 × 6
video_script.payoff_line: Each term is one part of the story.

final_answer.spoken: stories vary, and the values are one hundred, fifty four and forty eight

maths_rules: 5 x 12 - 6: 5 packets of 12 biscuits, 6 are eaten; 5 x 12 = 60, 60 - 6 = 54
4 x 9 + 2 x 6: 4 boxes of 9 mangoes and 2 bags of 6 mangoes; 36 + 12 = 48
video_script.design: One idea: one term for each part of the story. The three expressions stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the story and the value of each. Many stories are correct.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, a shop has eighty nine pencils.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty one more pencils come in.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ten pencils are sold.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Eighty nine plus twenty one is one hundred and ten.
One hundred and ten minus ten is one hundred.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>Five times twelve is sixty, and sixty minus six is fifty four.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, there are four boxes with nine mangoes in each.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>There are also two bags with six mangoes in each.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Four times nine is thirty six, and two times six is twelve.
The sum is forty eight.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check each story by going back.
One hundred pencils, less the twenty one that came, plus the ten sold, is eighty nine.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifty four biscuits plus the six eaten is sixty, which is five times twelve.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Forty eight mangoes less the twelve in the bags is thirty six, which is four times nine.

beats.on_screen: Answer: stories vary; the values are (a) 100 (b) 54 (c) 48
